GLM-5.3 scored 28.3 on Terminal-Bench 3.0 and 66.9 on DeepSWE v1.1 in Z.ai's own published results, but it trails the top frontier models on both. Every figure is vendor-reported, and no independent lab has re-run them under one harness.

- **Terminal-Bench 3.0:** The score rose from GLM-5.2's 4.6 to 28.3 (GLM-5.3 improves from 4.6 to 28.3 on Terminal-Bench 3.0). Z.ai's table lists GPT-5.6 Sol at 34.6 and Claude Fable 5 at 33.7 on the same benchmark.
- **DeepSWE v1.1:** The score rose from 46.2 to 66.9. Competitors are 72.7 for GPT-5.6 Sol and 69.7 for Fable 5. One comparison table also lists Kimi K3 at 67.5, slightly ahead of GLM-5.3 (DeepSWE (v1.1) | 66.9 | 46.2 | 67.5 | 58.0 | 72.7).
- **Caveats:** Some sources describe 28.3 as the best open-source score on Terminal-Bench 3.0, while others say Kimi K3 leads on DeepSWE. Terminal-Bench 2.1 and 3.0 are different exams, so cross-version comparisons are not valid. Z.ai ran its evaluations with its own harnesses and settings.

The results consistently report Qwen3.8-27B at 73.0 on Terminal-Bench 2.1 and 42.2 on DeepSWE 1.1. These numbers come from Alibaba's own model card, as relayed by secondary blogs, so I found no independent verification.

- **Scores vs. predecessor:** Qwen3.8-27B roughly triples Qwen3.6-27B's DeepSWE 1.1 score (42.2 vs. 13.3), while its Terminal-Bench 2.1 score rose from 63.4 to 73.0. The official model card shows Terminal-Bench 2.1 rising from 63.4 to 73.0, DeepSWE 1.1 from 13.3 to 42.2.
- **Comparison to Claude:** Opus 4.6 Max leads on Terminal-Bench 2.1 (78.2 vs. 73.0), and its DeepSWE cell is blank in the card. The viral claim that the 27B "beats Opus 4.7 on DeepSWE, 42.2 vs 40" has no basis in the model card: the Opus cell for DeepSWE 1.1 is literally a dash.
- **Other frontier comparisons:** One blog lists DeepSeek V4 Flash at 82.7 on Terminal-Bench 2.1 and 54.4 on DeepSWE 1.1, and GPT-5.6 Sol at 88.8 and 72.7, both well above Qwen3.8-27B. Qwen3.8-27B vs DeepSeek V4 Flash 0731, GPT-5.6 Sol, and a Claude comparator table appears in that source, and I could not confirm those figures against a primary source.
- **Methodology:** One source notes that DeepSWE uses Claude Code at 256K context. Treat cross-vendor comparisons with caution, since harnesses and settings differ.

The results give a mixed picture, and the figures come from different test setups, so they aren't directly comparable.

- **Vals AI** lists GPT-6 Luna at 13.64% on Terminal-Bench 4.0 and 4.29% on Terminal-Bench Science. Its Terminal-Bench 2.1 score is 73.03%, ranked #22 of 73. [vals.ai]

- **Kingy AI** says OpenAI did not publish a Terminal-Bench 4.0 score for GPT-6 Sol or Luna, and its comparison table leaves those cells blank. [kingy.ai]
- **Artificial Analysis's coding-agent write-up** says GPT-6 Luna (max) scored 41 on its Coding Agent Index, down 2 points from GPT-5.6 Luna, but gives no Luna-specific Terminal-Bench figure in the excerpt. [artificialanalysis.ai]
- **Benchmark sites** also list GPT-5.6 Luna (a predecessor) at about 84.7% on Terminal-Bench 2.1 (OpenAI-reported) and 17.3% on Terminal-Bench 4.0. Don't mix these with GPT-6 Luna numbers. [datalearner.com, benchlm.ai]

Bottom line: the GPT-6 Luna Terminal-Bench 4.0 scores I found range from roughly 1.5% to 13.6% depending on the evaluator and effort setting. Terminal-Bench 2.1 results are reported only by Vals AI, and the sources don't agree on the Luna naming. Check the original leaderboards before relying on any single number.

content.text:
I found every DeepSWE score, but the Terminal-Bench numbers can't go in one column. The labs report different versions of it (2.1, 3.0 and 4.0), and their scales are very different: 2.1 scores are in the 70s–90s, while 3.0 and 4.0 scores are mostly below 45. So the matrix gives each version its own column.

| Model | DeepSWE v1.1 | Terminal-Bench 2.1 | Terminal-Bench 3.0 | Terminal-Bench 4.0 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **GPT-6 Sol** | 68.8 (max effort)¹ | 83.2 (Vals) | — | 44.4 (Vals)² |
| **GPT-6 Luna** | 66.6 (max effort)¹ | 73.0 (Vals) | — | 13.6 (Vals)² |
| **Qwen3.8-27B** | 42.2 | 73.0 | — | — |
| **GLM-5.3** | 66.9 | — | 28.3 | — |
| **DeepSeek V4.1 Flash** | **74.2** | **90.6** | 30.0 | 31.2³ |

"—" means I couldn't find a published score.

**Where the numbers come from and what to watch for:**
- **DeepSWE:** every score is reported by the company that made the model, and no independent group has re-run them under a single setup. The DeepSWE results show both GPT-6 models are very sensitive to reasoning effort:
  - Sol: 37.2 / 56.6 / 65.3 / 66.6 / 68.8 (low, medium, high, xhigh, max)
  - Luna: 2.4 / 44.5 / 59.3 / 61.3 / 66.6
- **Terminal-Bench for GPT-6:** OpenAI didn't publish any Terminal-Bench scores for Sol or Luna. The figures above come from Vals AI's independent runs at max effort.
- **² Vals disagrees with itself:** its Sept 22 update lists lower Terminal-Bench 4.0 scores than its main table: Sol 34.3, Luna 9.6.
- **³** The DeepSeek 4.0 score comes from a single secondary source, so treat it as soft. Its 2.1 and DeepSWE scores match DeepSeek's technical report and NVIDIA's model card.
- **Qwen3.8-27B:** the numbers come from Alibaba's model card, passed along by blogs. A widely shared claim that it "beats Opus on DeepSWE" is wrong: the Opus cell in that table is blank.
- **Possible mix-up:** GPT-6.1 Sol is a different model. It reportedly scores about 75.2 on DeepSWE, so check which Sol you need.

**Takeaway:** on the numbers available, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash leads both benchmarks. GPT-6 Sol is next, with GLM-5.3 and GPT-6 Luna close together on DeepSWE. Qwen3.8-27B trails, though it's much smaller than the others. Even so, all the DeepSWE scores and most of the Terminal-Bench scores are self-reported, and the labs used different test setups, so the comparison is rough.
